Author: Sunil Kumar Awasthi
Bench: Sunil Kumar Awasthi

-( 1 )-
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Cr.R. No.3182/2017
 (Brajmohan Gupta Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh)
 Shri Navneet Kishore Verma, learned counsel for
the applicant.

Shri Gaurav Kumar Verma, learned Public
Prosecutor for the respondent/State.

Order 
(28/01/2020) The appellant /accused has been convicted for the commission of offence under Section 7(1) (3) and Section 14 (1) R/w 16(1) (A) (I) R/w 2 and Section 16 (1) (C) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred as 'Act, 1954") and sentenced to 3 months R.I. and fine of Rs. 1,000/- each with default stipulation vide judgment dated 19.08.2011 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, District Badwani in Criminal Case No.430/2009.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, District Badwani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In criminal appeal No.96/2011, the Special Judge, Badwani dismissed the criminal appeal vide judgment dated 03.11.2017.
Being aggrieved with the aforesaid judgment, this criminal revision has been preferred by the applicant.

(2). The facts of the case are that on 18.09.2007, the Food Inspector K.S. Solanki visited the shop of firm Brajmohan Radhakrishna situated at Ranjeet Chowk, Badwani and purchased three bottles of 500 ML of groundnut oil and paid Rs. 120/- to the present applicant who was present at the shop at the time of inspection; sealed them at the spot and sent them to Public Analyst for examination.

After examination the -( 2 )-
Public Analyst disclosed that the oil was not up to the standard prescribed by the rule as given in the Apenndix-B and it described as adulterated.
Thereafter, permission of prosecution was obtained from the concerned authority and complaint was filed before the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Badwani.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Badwani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Then notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was also sent to the applicant which served upon him on 14.06.2008.
(3). The applicant/accused absurd his guilt and examined himself as defence witness.

sentences.text: (4). The learned Magistrate First Class, Badwani after considering the prosecution evidence convicted and sentenced the applicant as mentioned above.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, the applicant has preferred an appeal before the Sessions Court and same was also dismissed in toto.
These orders are subject matter of challenge in the present revision petition.

(5). 
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that some packed sample was collected in which the name of the manufacturer was mentioned but he has not been implicated as party in the proceedings.
It is also submitted that although the report of food analyst disclosed that sample was found adulterated but no specific action of adulteration has been mentioned in the report.

It is further submitted that complaint has been filed after lapse of 9 months and therefore he had deprived of his statutory right under Section 13 (2) of the Act for sent part of sample to the Central Food Laboratory for further examination.

It is also submitted that if the report of the Public Analyst is accepted in its face value even then the sample was marginal away -( 3 )-
from the standard and therefore it cannot be said that the sample taken from the applicant is adulterated.
Under these circumstances, he prays for setting aside of the judgment of the courts below.

(6). Learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted according to the Public Analyst report the sample was found to be adulterated and courts below have properly appreciated the evidence and convicted the applicant for the said offence, therefore, there is no ground is available to interfere in the concurrent findings of the courts below, hence, he prays for dismissal of the revision petition.
(7). Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

(8). After considering the prosecution evidence, it would be apparent that testimony of the Food Inspector, K.S. Solanki (PW-1) is accepted to the effect that he purchased three bottles of groundnut oil containing 300 ML each, sealed them at the spot and sent them to Public Analyst, Bhopal for examination.
According to the Public Analyst report, the same was found adulterated.
He also given notice under Section 13(2) of the Act to the present applicant but he did not apply for analysis for the sample from the Central Food Laboratory.

(9). Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that there is marginal error in the various results obtained by the Public Analyst in the sample which was examined by him and it may be compared with the standard as mentioned in the Appendix -B of the the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 at Article A.
-( 4 )-
17.03.

In that specification, it was mentioned that the groundnut oil should be clear, free from rancidity, suspended or other foreign matter, separated water, added colouring or flavouring substances, or mineral oil and it should conform to the following standards:-

2  Exh.P-18 (a) Butyro- refractometer reading 54.0 to 57.1 58.2  41 C  or  Refractive Index at 40  C 1.4620-1.460 (b) Saponification value 188 to 196 189.63 (c) Iodine value 85 to 99 109.68 (d) Insaponifiable matter Not more than --  1.0 percent (e) Acid Value Not more than 1.97  6.0 (f) Bellier test (Turbidity 39  C to 41  C 37. 0  C temperature-Acetic Acid method) Test for argemone oil shall be negative

After comparison on the basis of extract of the report (Exh.P-18) and standard given article A-17.3 of the rules, it appears that Butyro-refractometer reading is higher more than 1.1 % than the standard.
Iodine value is higher 10% than the standard value.
Billier Test (turbidity Temperature - Acetic Acid Method) lower than the standard, whereas remaining reading were within limits as shown by the standard.
No other oil was found mixed in the sample.

(10). The Food Inspector purchased 3 packed bottles containing 500 ML each and one packed bottle sent to the Public Analyst whereas two bottles were kept in safe custody in the office of appropriate -( 5 )-
authority and on examination the food analyst found the complete sample of the groundnut bottle as adulterated, therefore, it cannot be said that the sample was taken by the Food Inspector without churning and it was not properly stirred.

(11). Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the judgment passed by Single Bench of this Court in the case of Ramesh Chandra Vs. State of M.P. 2014(3) M.P. H.T.382 and Beni Prasad State of M.P. 2004 (1) MPWN 201 in which there was marginal error slightly difference in the various readings between the sample and the standard fixed by the P.F. Rules, therefore, this Court was of the view that sample cannot be adulterated.

sentences.text:
However, in the present case there is much difference in various readings found in comparison with the standard fixed by P.F. Rules and there are no possibility of improper stirring of oil before taking the sample because a complete sealed bottle of groundnut oil was purchased and sent to the Public Analyst for analyzing, therefore,
aforesaid judgment is distinguishable in the fact of the present case.
(12) In the instant case, the sample was taken on 18.09.2007 and it was examined by the Public Analyst on 24.10.2007,
therefore, it cannot be said that the groundnut oil was remained with the Public Analyst for long period for testing.

In the present case the complaint was filed by the Food Inspector on 09.06.2008 within 9 months of taking of sample from the applicant and before this a notice was under Section 13 (2) Act was also served upon the applicant and he was having an opportunity to apply to the court for -( 6 )-
Brajmohan Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123613087/
3 getting it examined through Central Food Laboratory.

sentences.text: But after appearing before the trial court he did not filed any application for sending the second sample of the groundnut oil for further examination by the Central Food Laboratory, therefore, applicant cannot take plea that complaint was filed after 9 months of taking sample, thus the sample of groundnut oil was not fit for analysis by the Central Food Laboratory.

If the applicant applied for the same and Central Food Laboratory opined that now the sample is not fit for analysis then the applicant can take plea that he deprived for his statutory right conferred under Sub Section 2 of Section of 13 of the Act.

(13). In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court finds that the courts below have not committed any error in convicting the appellant for the said offence and there is minimum sentence is prescribed for the offence committed by the applicant, thus, there is no reason for reducing the sentence awarded to the applicant by the trial court as well as appellate court.
Hence, present revision application is hereby dismissed by affirming conviction and sentenced passed by the courts below.
Applicant is on bail, he is directed to surrender before the trial court immediately so that he can send into custody for serving his remaining jail sentence.
14. Let a copy of this Order be sent to the concerned courts alongwith the records.
